stimulus.text: The painting, attributed to Frederick Kemmelmeyer and made after 1795, shows George Washington on a white horse reviewing the Western Army at Fort Cumberland, Maryland. Washington points toward long ranks of soldiers in blue coats, with a cannon at the left and mountains behind them.

stem: Why was whiskey so important to the grain farmers of western Pennsylvania?

options.text: Whiskey was the only drink the Constitution allowed them to make.
options.misconception: Background: the Constitution did not regulate what farmers could drink or make.

options.text: Distilling grain into whiskey made it compact, valuable, and easy to carry.
Whiskey was the currency the federal government used to pay its debts.
options.misconception: Background: the government paid its debts with bonds and money, not with whiskey.

options.text: Whiskey was the main crop the British bought from the western counties.
options.misconception: Background: the farmers sold whiskey at home and in the east, not mainly to Britain.

rationales.B: Background: grain was bulky and roads were poor, so turning it into whiskey raised its value and made it easier to carry.
rationales.A: The Constitution is not about what farmers may make.
rationales.C: The government did not pay its debts in whiskey.
rationales.D: The farmers’ market was not mainly Britain.
rationales.general:
1. The rebellion broke out among grain farmers in the far west of Pennsylvania.
2. Background: their grain was bulky and the roads were poor, so hauling it east cost more than it was worth.
3. Distilling the grain into whiskey shrank it, raised its value, and made it easy to carry.
4. So a tax on whiskey struck at the one way these farmers could turn a crop into cash.
Remember: on a frontier, what matters is how a crop travels, not only how it grows.
